product.title: O săptămână cu susul în jos
product.description: De la cel mai bine cotat autor internațional al momentului, Carl-Johan Forssén Ehrlin, autorul bestsellerelor Elefănțelul care nu voia să adoarmă și Tractorașul care nu voia să adoarmă, o nouă carte pentru copii inspirată de psihologia comportamentalăTudor este un băiețel ca oricare altul. Îi place să se cațăre în copaci, să se plimbe cu bicicleta și să se joace cu prietenii. Familia sa tocmai s-a mutat într-un oraș nou și, în prima săptămână după mutare, prietenul nostru încearcă o mulțime de emoții noi, pe care nu le-a mai simțit înainte și...totul pare că merge pe dos! O săptămână cu susul în jos nu este o carte obișnuită. Inspirat de psihologia comportamentală și de tehnici de comunicare – schimbarea culorii durerii pentru a o putea diminua, modificarea unei imagini mentale pentru a transforma sentimentele pe care le provoacă, înlocuirea fluxului de emoții negative cu unele pozitive etc –, volumul le va oferi copiilor instrumentele de care au nevoie pentru a gestiona mai ușor situațiile de zi cu zi. Totodată, îi învață pe adulți să comunice mai bine și să-i îndrume pe cei mici în momentele dificile.

# A Week Upside Down: Navigating Emotions and Growth

**Brand:** Litera
**Category:** Children's Books
**Price:** 44.99

The emotional landscape of childhood can be unpredictable, especially when facing major life changes like moving or starting a new school year. *A Week Upside Down* is a powerful and insightful story designed to help young readers understand the complex world of feelings. From the highly acclaimed international author Carl-Johan ForssÃ©n Ehrlin (bestseller author of *The Elephant Who Didn't Want to Sleep*), this book goes beyond simple storytelling, offering inspiration rooted in behavioral psychology and advanced communication techniques.

Discover how Tudor, a boy who loves adventure, navigates his first week in a new city. Like many children, he is overwhelmed by a flood of unfamiliar emotionsâit truly feels like everything is going "upside down." This book provides the emotional toolkit that both children and parents need to manage these difficult periods with understanding and resilience.

## ð§  Tools for Emotional Resilience and Communication

*A Week Upside Down* is not just a bedtime story; it's a guide to developing emotional intelligence. The narrative structure introduces foundational concepts from behavioral psychology, teaching children practical methods for dealing with overwhelming feelings:

*   **Emotional Reframing:** Learn how to visualize and "change the color of pain" or modify negative mental images to transform challenging emotions into manageable ones.
*   **Positive Coping Mechanisms:** The book systematically replaces negative emotional patterns with positive affirmations and coping strategies, giving children tangible tools for daily life.
*   **Parental Guidance:** Importantly, the volume also serves as a resource for adults. It equips parents with better communication techniques, helping them guide their young ones through moments of difficulty with confidence and empathy.

By following Tudor's journey, readers will gain a deeper understanding of emotional regulationâa critical skill that empowers children to face transitions and challenges head-on.

## Why Choose This Book for Your Child?

This title is ideal for parents looking for educational literature that addresses modern parenting concerns: anxiety related to change, developing self-awareness, and improving family communication. It turns abstract psychological concepts into an engaging, relatable story for young minds.

***

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Is this book only for children?**
No. While the narrative follows a child's perspective, the themes and techniques discussed are highly valuable for parents and caregivers, offering actionable insights into improving family communication during times of stress or transition.

**What age group is this most suitable for?**
The concepts are accessible to young readers who are experiencing life changes (e.g., moving, starting school). However, because it touches on behavioral psychology, it can be read and discussed with children in the preschool through early elementary grades.
